title: macOS artifact ships a dangling @cubric/connector symlink; the documented xattr command errors for every user
description: package.json:27 declares "@cubric/connector": "file:../Cubric-Studio/packages/connector", so npm creates app/node_modules/@cubric/connector as a symlink to a SIBLING REPO on the dev machine. The macOS build archives with ditto, which faithfully preserves symlinks, so the shipped zip carries a link to ../../../Cubric-Studio/packages/connector that can never resolve on a user machine. Windows and Linux artifacts contain NOTHING at that path (their packagers drop it), so this is macOS-only. IMPACT IS NOT A CRASH: all three consumers load it via dynamic import inside try/catch (server.js:143, services/brokerBoot.js:61 which explicitly returns null with "SDK not installed in this build", services/connectorResponder.js:80). The real cost is UX and trust - our own documented first-run instruction xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <folder> prints "xattr: No such file: .../app/node_modules/@cubric/connector" for EVERY Mac user, who reasonably concludes the download is broken. FOUND LIVE 2026-07-31 on the rented M4; it was xattr that surfaced it, and an earlier dangling-symlink check missed it because that check was scoped to Electron.app only. FIX: exclude the file: dependency from the packaged node_modules, or dereference it at build time.
